content.title: S&P 500 Movers: Equifax Hits Back At FICO In Credit Score Wars
content.summary: Equifax has slashed prices for mortgage credit scores in response to Fair Isaac's move last week that aimed to limit the mortgage industry's reliance on credit bureaus.  FICO was the biggest laggard on the S&P 500, giving back a big chunk of last week's gains, while Equifax recovered some of last week's losses.  The backdrop is that FICO has been under pressure from Bill Pulte, director of the Federal Housing Finance Agency, who said in July that government-backed mortgage giants Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac will now allow lenders to use VantageScore 4.0 as an alternative to the traditional FICO score.

content.title: Equifax Strikes Back in Battle of the Credit Scores. Fair Isaac Stock Tumbles.
content.summary: Less than a week after  Fair Isaac  moved to bypass the three nationwide credit bureaus and distribute FICO scores directly to mortgage lenders,  Equifax  struck back.  Equifax  announced that it would make the VantageScore 4.0—an alternative to the FICO score—available for $4.50 a score over the next two years.  The company also will provide VantageScore for free to all  Equifax  customers who purchase FICO scores in 2025 and 2026.

content.title: Hack Your Credit Score: More People Are Using Rent Payments As the New Secret Weapon For FICO Boosts
content.summary: Your monthly rent could do more than just keep a roof over your head. It can also help you build credit. Recent data from TransUnion shows a noticeable jump in the number of people who plan to or already are self-reporting their rent payments. The number of consumers whose rent payments are reported to credit reporting agencies rose to 13% in 2025, up from 11% in 2024, according to the report.
